title: Fire and flood management of coastal swamp enabled first rice paddy cultivation in east China
lineage: Original palaeoecological study of an excavation-face sediment sequence and associated archaeological contexts.

passages.note: The authors place their studied cultural sediments in a modelled interval of about 7700–7550 cal BP. This interpretation concerns one excavated sequence.

Pollen, algal and fungal indicators, diatoms and microscopic charcoal are used to infer sustained wetland rice cultivation. Clearance and later maintenance are interpretations of changes in vegetation and fire indicators. Low-level brackish inflow is observed indirectly; a protective barrier is hypothesised.
